extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and practitioners preparing and submitting papers to IAAI-25 (authors of applied AI papers)
extracted.subtask_description: Call-for-papers and submission rules for IAAI-25, a venue for innovative applications of AI. Includes track-specific evaluation criteria, formatting and originality requirements, and supplementary/materials and review policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / simultaneous submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must be original. IAAI-25 will not consider any paper that, at the time of submission, is under review for or has already been published or accepted for publication in a journal or another conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These restrictions apply only to refereed journals and conferences, not to preliminary versions posted as preprints to arXiv.org or other unrefereed forums, or to workshops with a limited audience and without archival proceedings. Once submitted to IAAI-25, authors may not submit the paper elsewhere during IAAI’s review period. Authors must confirm that their submissions conform to these requirements at the time of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format and formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic submissions are required. Papers must be in trouble-free, high resolution PDF format and formatted for United States letter (8.5" x 11") paper. Submissions need to be in AAAI two-column format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CameraReady templates in the AAAI 2025 Author Kit. We cannot accept papers submitted by email or fax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits and references page policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Deployed papers can be up to eight (8) pages plus one more page containing only references. Emerging, Tools and Integration papers can be up to six (6) pages plus one more page containing only references. Best practice, Challenge, and Training papers may be up to (6) pages long, plus one more page containing only references. Papers of at most two (2) pages, plus one more page containing only references, may also be submitted and considered exclusively for presentation as a poster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At most one additional page beyond the limits may contain only references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material in the form of (1) technical appendix, (2) multimedia, (3) code and data may be submitted alongside all papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main submission may reference the supplementary material but should be self-contained. Reviewers will be instructed to make their acceptance evaluations based on the main submission and will not be obliged to consult the supplementary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author identification and review model
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to IAAI-25 should contain identifying information of the authors and their affiliations: reviewing is single-blind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is also recommended to add authors from the deploying institutions as co-authors to show the real-world impact of the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline and eligibility enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions received after the deadline, or that do not meet the length or formatting requirements detailed above, will not be accepted for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: all deadlines are “anywhere on earth” (UTC-12). Authors will receive notification emails; authors must transfer copyright for accepted papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deployed applications eligibility (definition of 'deployed')
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted to this track must describe deployed applications with measurable benefits that include an innovative use of AI technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are defined as deployed once they are in production use by their final end-users and the in-use experience can be meaningfully collected and reported. The study may evaluate either a stand-alone application or a component of a complex system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deployed track evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers will be judged by the quality of: the task or problem description; the application description; the innovative use of AI technology; the measurable application use and payoff; and the lessons learned during application development, deployment and maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-depth descriptions of the algorithm are generally more appropriate for AAAI than for IAAI. Each accepted deployed application paper will receive the IAAI ‘Innovative Application’ Award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emerging applications track requirements and evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Emerging applications papers 'bridge the gap' between basic AI research and case studies of deployed AI applications; a key requirement for papers is to discuss the path forward for achieving deployment of the technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers will be judged primarily by: significance (of the problem, and the tool or methodology); relevance of AI technology to the problem; innovation; path to deployment; content; evaluation; technical quality; and clarity. Authors are advised to consider the novelty of applying AI to the particular problem domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deployed Innovative Tools track evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers will be judged primarily by the extent to which the tool presented yields solutions with demonstrated improved quality; lower development, deployment and maintenance costs; better productivity; fewer errors; and higher ability to scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will pay attention to how well designed is the tool, how easy is it to use and how well is it documented, and how many users it has. Note the focus is on the tool, not on foundational research. Areas of interest include process organization, data cleaning, modelling, meta-algorithmics, platforms, novel computational models, interaction, and trusted AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative inter-disciplinary AI integration expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: This track is devoted to the integration of AI components with the focus on how the orchestration of methods from different AI silos requires the adaptation of existing technologies to allow them to work together well for application of AI in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers must pay attention to engineering considerations and, where relevant, to human–computer interaction. A clear, transparent, and reproducible case must be presented that allows the community to judge objectively the value of the innovation of the integration when compared to existing or ad-hoc approaches. Computational experiments on benchmarks (that either already are or will be made public) and in comparison with existing state-of-the-art baseline methods are expected. At least a portion of the experiments is expected to consider real-world (not synthetic generated) benchmarks to demonstrate the practical importance of the problem studied.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI Incidents and Best Practices track requirements and review focus
rubrics_metrics.description: These papers must (a) analyze the development and deployment processes and artifacts in relation to harms realized in the real world for one or more AI incidents, (b) analyze AI incident trends to understand where there are open problems in the deployment of AI systems, and/or (c) detail best practices in producing and deploying systems to prevent or mitigate AI incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers will be reviewed by a program committee of AI, human factors, safety, and ethics researchers with a particular focus on whether the paper informs the safe practice of deploying intelligent systems in the world. All papers will be added to the AI Incident Database for the referenced AI incidents. Papers in this track may be up to (6) pages long; papers of at most two (2) pages may also be submitted and considered exclusively for presentation as a poster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer evaluation basis (main submission emphasizes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will be instructed to make their acceptance evaluations based on the main submission and will not be obliged to consult the supplementary material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main submission should therefore be self-contained even if supplementary materials (technical appendix, multimedia, code and data) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to include deploying-institution authors
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended to add authors from the deploying institutions as co-authors to show the real-world impact of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recommendation supports demonstrating practical deployment and impact in 'deployed' and applied papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper awards criteria (Festo Best Use of AI in Industrial Engineering)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Festo Best use of AI in Industrial Engineering award recognizes the most innovative use of AI in designing, building, and programming automation solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should demonstrate creative AI applications in areas such as deep learning, big data analysis, and smart manufacturing. The top paper receives monetary and travel support prizes and potential additional opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper awards criteria (DSRI AI Incidents and Best Practices Paper Award)
rubrics_metrics.description: The DSRI AI Incidents and Best Practices Paper Award recognizes outstanding contributions in analyzing AI incidents and showcasing best practices for preventing or mitigating their recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award acknowledges research that deepens understanding of factors related to AI incidents, identifies open problems in deployment, and offers valuable insights and guidelines for safe production and deployment of systems.
